subject: QBR: Pipeline snapshot + owner playbook (prep)
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: QBR: Pipeline snapshot + owner playbook (prep)

Team —

We need a compact package for the QBR: a one-tab pipeline snapshot for the exec deck and an account-by-account playbook that sales owners can use during the readout. Goal is to have a clean rollup by EOD Friday so leadership can rehearse Monday.

Ask: please contribute your sections into the attached workbook and the playbook PDF template. Specifics below:

- Laura: can you refresh the closes-by-date and mark anything that requires leader attention (blockers, legal/PO delays)?
- Marissa: fold in the commit/non-commit split and the most likely CMR (close-mostly-rate) by owner.
- Vivek: add the OKR alignment notes per named account (which OKR this deal helps and expected delivery quarter).

Attachments: QBR_pipeline_snapshot_ACME_0626.xlsx (xlsx) — workbook with three tabs: rollup, owner-breakouts, raw-opps; Account-by-account_playbook_ACME.pdf (pdf) — playbook template; Deck_QBR_pipeline_rollup_v3.pptx (pptx) — slide stub for execs.

Quick format guidance for the playbook section per account (one paragraph + 3 bullets):
- Current stage & expected close date
- Key blockers / dependencies (legal, data residency, infra)
- Next 72h owner asks (who will do what)

Timing: populate the sheet and reply with the updated attachment by Friday 6/26 5pm PT. If you need a second set of eyes I can pair with you Thursday afternoon.

Thanks —
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Commercial Strategy | Redwood Inference
jonas@redwood.com

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com, vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 25 Jun 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: Pipeline snapshot + owner playbook (prep)

Jonas —

Thanks. I'm on this. Quick notes from a scan of the attached rollup:

- Two deals (ACME — Cloud Migration, ACME — Dedicated GPUs) are flagged as at-risk due to PO timing from procurement. I've added a red tag in the "owner-breakouts" tab and a short rationale column.
- For slides, I'll condense the closes-by-date to a 6-week view (to keep exec focus on runway).
- Need confirmation on whether we want to include churn-adjusted ARR in the rollup; that changes the net commit numbers.

I'm attaching the updated workbook with my owner notes and the red/amber flags. See the "notes_for_leadership" cell on tab 'rollup' for suggested speaking points.

Attachment: QBR_pipeline_snapshot_ACME_0626.xlsx (updated)

One more ask: legal has requested an MSA amendment for the Dedicated GPUs deal — that's blocking signature. Can we route an escalation if payment terms won't be adjusted by Thursday?

Laura Bennett
Sr. Manager, Enterprise Accounts | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, laura_bennett@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 26 Jun 2026 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: QBR: Pipeline snapshot + owner playbook (prep)

Nice work — a couple of framing points for leadership I added inline in the doc and below:

- OKR tie: the Cloud Migration deal should be framed as directly contributing to OKR 2.1 (Reduce inference latency for enterprise workloads) because their rollout accelerates our latency-sensitive benchmarks for the region. Call this out on slide 2.
- Forecast discipline: separate 'committed' from 'best case' in the single-number slide. Use commit for the baseline and a bounded upside.
- Risk-adjusted probability: for the exec rollup include a one-line justification for any >$500k opportunity using the following matrix: owner confidence, procurement timing, legal signoff.

I'm adding the OKR mapping as a short column in the 'owner-breakouts' tab. Also uploaded two suggested speaking bullets for each high-dollar account.

Vivek Kulkarni
VP, Sales Operations | Redwood Inference
vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com

- Consolidated forecast into three lines on the rollup slide: Commit (total $1.85M), Probable (upside $420k), and Pipeline (total $3.7M). Numbers are net of expected churn. See row 5 on 'rollup' tab.
- Added owner-by-owner closing plan: Laura (Cloud Migration — ACME) now has a procurement escalation plan and a named legal contact (T. Fernandes, acme-legal@acmecorp.com).
- For ACME accounts I added short owner playbook entries: 1) Executive sponsor mapping, 2) Delivery gating items (network/hsm), 3) 72h asks.

Attachments uploaded: Account-by-account_playbook_ACME.pdf (final), QBR_pipeline_snapshot_ACME_0626.xlsx (final), Deck_QBR_pipeline_rollup_v3.pptx (updated with commit numbers).

Next: Jonas — can you route the procurement/legal escalation for the Dedicated GPUs deal on Monday morning? Laura and I are aligned on the ask and timeline.

Thanks everyone — feel free to pull me into rehearsal if helpful.

Marissa Cole
